1: [Sermon on the Eternal Birth — The birth in the soul]

We are celebrating the feast of the Eternal Birth which God the Father has borne and never ceases to bear in the soul — if only the soul is prepared. For the Father begets His Son in the soul in the same manner as He begets Him in eternity, neither more nor less: in the innermost part of the soul the birth takes place, and the soul is the Bethlehem of the second nativity.
[Sermon on the Eternal Birth — The nobleman]

There is a nobleman in the soul whom no enemy has ever yet taken, and in whom God the Father bears His Son without ceasing. And the nobleman is so noble that nothing is nobler; and he is so poor that nothing is poorer; and he is so hidden that nothing is more present — and all three are one.
[Sermon on the Eternal Birth — The word]

The soul that would hear the word must be still as a desert. All creatures cry out to God, but the soul that is silent hears what the creatures are crying: that God is their ground, and they are His speech.
2: [Sermon on the Poor in Spirit — True poverty]

A man is truly poor who wants nothing, knows nothing, and has nothing. He who wants nothing is as God wants; he who knows nothing has returned into the ignorance from which he came; and he who has nothing is the temple where God dwells — for God made the temple for Himself alone.
[Sermon on the Poor in Spirit — The eye]
The eye with which I see God is the same eye with which God sees me: one seeing, one knowing, one loving. And the seer and the seen are one thing in the ground, though they are two in the world.
[Sermon on the Poor in Spirit — The God beyond God]

I pray God to rid me of God. For the God of my images is small, and I have made Him with my hands, and I must let Him go, as a child lets go of its picture of the sun when the sun itself rises. And what remains when the picture is gone — that is God, and I am in Him, and He is in me, and there is no fear left.
3: All things are the more or less the angels, and the angels are the more or less the face of God. Therefore despise nothing, not even the least thing, for in the least thing the whole of the face is looking at you, and it is looking with love.

He who is truly detached is unmoved by praise and unmoved by blame, as the mountain is unmoved by wind. And his works are not his own but God's; and therefore they prosper, though the man himself does not watch them prosper.

I say that God is indistinguishable from myself: I am in God, and if I depart, God must follow. The eye in which I am caught is His eye, and the breakthrough of the soul into God is the same as God's breaking into the soul — and both breakthroughs happen in the same still point, and the still point is now.
